newsitem.title: USA: Drug cocktail useful against a type of leukemia.
newsitem.headline: Drug cocktail useful against a type of leukemia.

text.p: A team of French doctors reports in Thursday's New England Journal of Medicine that adding the drug cytarabine to a mix of two others can improve the survival rate for those suffering from chronic myelogenous leukaemia, a blood cancer that typically afflicts mature adults.
Chronic myelogenous leukaemia, or CML, strikes about one out of every 50,000 Americans annually.

The French team wrote in Thursday's New England Journal of Medicine that the 360 patients who received the cytarabine along with the conventional medicines used - hydroxyurea and interferon alfa - had a death rate that was 36 percent lower than the rate for the 361 who received only the conventional drugs.
But cytarabine, sold under the brand name Cytosar-U by Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc., produced so many side effects it was discontinued in 94 of the 360 patients who took it.

The most common problems were nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and an inflammation of the body's mucous membranes. It also reduced the number of clot-forming platelets in the blood, but there were no cases of life-threatening bleeding among the volunteers, according to the team, led by Dr. Francois Guilhot of Jean Bernard Hospital in Poitiers.

The best treatment continues to be a bone marrow transplant, which prolongs survival in as many as 70 percent of patients. But some sufferers are too old for a transplant, or a suitable donor is unavailable.

For people who are not candidates for a transplant, "initial treatment with interferon alfa and cytarabine is an attractive option," Dr. John Goldman of the Royal Postgraduate Medical School in London said in an editorial in the Journal.
